## Introduction

Data repositories are good.
They theoretically encourage the reuse of data.
Some groups have found very, very cool ways to reuse and reanalyze transcriptomics data, for examples.
However, as with all data, and most especially -omics level data, there are issues with data quality.
As such, we have attempted to assess the quality of a large number of datasets in an open data repository where we are very familiar with the underlying data format, the Metabolomics Workbench.

Previous related publications include

The measures we have used to assess the quality include:
  * Higher correlation with samples between subject-sample-factors;
  * P-values of subject-sample-factors and sample principal component scores;
  * The number of outlier samples detected within each subject-sample-factor;
  * The correlations of any quality-control samples, if present.

We also provide quality-control reports for a large number of analyses.

In addition, for those analyses with a small number of subject-sample-factors, we attempt to recapture the experimental design, and then examine the MW analyses for cases where there is only a single factor present that perhaps is incorrect.
